title: response_transformer plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `response_transformer` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component ResponseTransformerConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

operation.description:
add: insert if absent (does not overwrite).
update: write, creating intermediate objects as needed.
remove: delete the field.
rename: move old → new, with rollback if the destination is unreachable.
Operation-incompatible extras are rejected: only add/update
may set `value`; only rename may set `new_key`; remove may
set neither.

key.description:
Dot-notation body path. Supports nested objects, array indexing
('items.0'), and backslash-escaped literal dots. Empty segments
(an empty path, or a leading, trailing, or doubled unescaped `.`)
are rejected. `rename` additionally rejects unescaped numeric
segments here and in `new_key`.

value.description:
Required for add/update; must not be set for remove/rename.
Accepts any JSON value — strings, numbers, booleans, objects,
arrays, and explicit null. Strings that parse as JSON
(e.g., "42", "true", '{"a":1}') are inserted as the parsed
type at runtime; otherwise kept as a JSON string.

new_key.description:
Required for rename; must not be set for add/update/remove.
Array indices and empty dot-segments are rejected in a rename
`key` / `new_key`.

ResponseTransformerConfig.description:
Plugin: response_transformer — Modifies response headers and JSON
body. Configuration is fail-closed: unknown top-level keys and
unknown per-rule keys are rejected at plugin load time. Header
rules enforce operation-exact fields (only add/update accept
`value`; only rename accepts `new_key`; remove accepts neither).
Protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing destinations are rejected
for add/update and as rename destinations (`Connection`,
`Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`,
`Trailer`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`, `Content-Length`,
case-insensitive); remove of those names remains allowed. The
gateway derives Content-Length and strips connection/framing
fields at the final H1/H2/H3 response boundary after every
mutable hook. Every configured header `value` must be a valid
HTTP `HeaderValue` (same complete syntax accepted at emission),
including rejection of non-CR/LF forbidden control bytes. Unknown
operations / targets and missing required fields are also
rejected. Every rule must set an explicit `target` (`header` or
`body`); there is no default. Valid targets are `header` and
`body` only — unlike request_transformer, there is no `query`
target.

Body-rule output above the effective response ceiling is refused with
HTTP 502 and the Response body too large JSON error with numeric limit, X-Gateway-Error:
overload, and error_class: dispatch_policy_rejected. One warning names
proxy id, plugin, ceiling, and the produced-size lower bound at the first
refused serializer write; no payload is logged. Exactly-at-ceiling
output passes. Aggregate retained-buffer exhaustion remains HTTP 503.

When `apply_route_overrides: true`, the plugin accepts an empty `rules`
array so it can participate in the chain-level response route-header
final phase for transforms published by `mesh_route_dispatch` onto
`RequestContext.route_override_response_transform`. Every enabled
instance applies only its static rules first; proxy core then applies
the matched route list exactly once after the last eligible instance.
The same composition contract as `request_transformer` applies on the
response side: the exact translator-owned empty-rule consumer is
ADDITIVE to a same-name global transformer (no shadowing, no warning),
while an ordinary operator-configured proxy-scoped instance replaces the
global.

At least one of a non-empty `rules` array or `apply_route_overrides:
true` is required: a config with no effect is rejected at plugin load
time. Per-operation required and forbidden properties are modelled in
the target-specific rule schemas below, by PRESENCE — an explicit `null`
fails exactly as a string would. Explicit `null` on an optional
top-level field is accepted and treated as absent.

apply_route_overrides.description:
Counterpart to `request_transformer.apply_route_overrides` for
response headers: accept empty `rules` and remain eligible for the
chain-level route-header finalization phase. Auto-emitted by the
Istio VirtualService translator on routes carrying
`headers.response.{set,add,remove}` that have no operator-configured
`response_transformer`, and by the Gateway API translator on rules
carrying `ResponseHeaderModifier`. With no
static `rules`, the instance's fail-closed response-trailer policy
applies only to requests whose matched `mesh_route_dispatch` rule
published a `response_transform`, so other requests on the same
proxy keep their backend trailers; any static rule makes that policy
apply to every response. Such a rules-free instance cannot carry a
per-instance `trigger`. Explicit `null` is accepted and treated as
`false`.

runtime_overlay_scope.description: Optional RTDS boolean key controlling whether the transformer runs. Must contain at least one non-whitespace character; surrounding whitespace is trimmed at runtime. Explicit `null` is accepted and treated as absent.

default_enabled.description: Fallback when `runtime_overlay_scope` is configured but the accepted RTDS overlay has no boolean value for that key. Explicit `null` is accepted and treated as absent (so the `true` default applies).

runtime_overlay_resolved_enabled.description: Reserved, mesh-managed. Counterpart to `RequestTransformerConfig.runtime_overlay_resolved_enabled`. Binding the gate to the generation is what keeps this plugin's buffering preflight and its later header/body hooks in agreement: a gate that moved between those phases could otherwise stream a response that had already been header-marked as transformed (GHSA-83rc-23c9-3g9x).

operation.description:
add: insert if absent (does not overwrite).
update: write the header value.
remove: delete the header.
rename: move old → new header name. Set-Cookie is rejected as
either source or destination (case-insensitive), regardless of
cookie count, because its multi-value representation is name-bound.
Operation-incompatible extras are rejected: only add/update
may set `value`; only rename may set `new_key`; remove may
set neither.

key.description:
HTTP header name; must be a complete HTTP field-name token (the same
grammar `HeaderName` accepts). For add/update, must not be a
protocol-managed
hop-by-hop or framing destination (`connection`, `content-length`,
`keep-alive`, `proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`, `te`,
`trailer`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`). Remove may target
those names. `rename` additionally rejects `set-cookie` as source.

value.description:
Required for add/update; must not be set for remove/rename.
Must be a valid HTTP HeaderValue (HTAB, visible ASCII, and
obs-text are accepted; CR, LF, DEL, and other C0 controls are
rejected).

new_key.description:
Required for rename; must not be set for add/update/remove.
Must be a complete HTTP field-name token, must not be `set-cookie`,
and must not be a protocol-managed hop-by-hop or framing destination
(`connection`, `content-length`, `keep-alive`,
`proxy-authenticate`, `proxy-connection`, `te`, `trailer`,
`transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`).

TransformerBodyRenamePath.description:
A dot-notation body path usable as a `rename` source or destination.
Array indices are rejected at plugin load time: rename over an array is
ambiguous (move? swap? overwrite?) and `Vec::remove`'s leftward shift
would silently drop a trailing element. Use `remove` + `add` to relocate
an array element. An ESCAPED numeric segment (`counts\.0` — a literal
key named `counts.0`) remains valid, so the exclusion applies only to an
unescaped path whose dot-delimited segments contain a plain integer.

TransformerOperationFieldExactness.description:
The operation-exact field contract both transformers enforce at plugin
load time, shared by every header / query / body rule schema: `add` and
`update` require `value` and forbid `new_key`; `rename` requires
`new_key` and forbids `value`; `remove` forbids both. Forbidden
properties are rejected by PRESENCE, so an explicit `null` fails exactly
as a string would. A body `value` may itself be `null` on `add` /
`update` — that sets the target field to JSON null.
